title: BatDeck - Ultra Low-power Ultrasonic Ego-velocity Estimation and Obstacle Avoidance on Nano-drones
summary: Preprint on arXiv (ETH Zurich and University of Bologna). Adds TDK ultrasonic sensors to a Crazyflie 2.1 for obstacle avoidance and ground velocity, and compares them in real office flights with a forward VL53L1 laser ToF on a Multi-ranger deck and with the Flow deck v2. With the VL53L1 all 10 flights crashed after 4 m on average, mostly on undetected glass doors.
key_takeaways: VL53L1 laser ToF misses glass doors and struggles with black objects
27 deg VL53L1 cone misses objects that fill little of it, such as a chair edge
Flow deck velocity degrades over a featureless table; fine over carpet

title: VL53L1X datasheet: long distance ranging Time-of-Flight sensor (STMicroelectronics)
summary: Datasheet for the 940 nm laser ToF chip used five times on the Crazyflie Multi-ranger deck and once on the Flow deck v2. Gives the 27 deg full field of view, programmable region of interest, short, medium and long distance modes and maximum range by ambient light and target reflectance. Revision not checked; the range table was read through secondary reproductions, not the PDF text.
key_takeaways: 27 deg full cone per sensor, reducible with a smaller SPAD region of interest
Long mode: about 3.6 m in the dark, about 0.73 m in strong ambient light
Short mode about 1.35 m in any light, up to 50 Hz

title: Go with the Flow: Relative Positioning with the Flow deck
summary: Bitcraze blog post on how the Flow deck v2 estimates position by dead reckoning in the onboard EKF and where it fails. Lists floor, light and motion conditions that make the estimate drift or diverge. Gives no drift-per-metre figure.
key_takeaways: Needs a textured, matte, well-lit floor; wood is best
Fails over plain or black floors, in low light and over its own shadow
Frequent yaw causes drift; do not fly too high
